newsitem.title: USA: U.S. renews Lebanon travel ban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. renews Lebanon travel ban.

text.p: The United States, rejecting appeals from Beirut, has renewed its ban on Americans travelling to Lebanon for another six months, the State Department said on Friday.

The decision by outgoing Secretary of State Warren Christopher dashed hopes raised at a U.S.-hosted conference last month designed to raise post-war reconstruction aid for Lebanon that the 12-year-old ban might be relaxed.

"We continue to have concerns about safety in Lebanon," State Department spokesman John Dinger said. "The secretary reviewed the passport restriction in this context and decided to continue the restriction."

The ban is next due for review by July 31, a decision that will fall to Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright, assuming she is confirmed by the Senate. Christopher leaves office next Monday.

Lebanese President Elias Hrawi urged the United States on Jan. 6 to lift the ban, which Washington imposed in 1985 after Moslem militants hijacked a U.S. airliner to Beirut and killed an American passenger.
The United States says it admires Lebanese government efforts to reconstruct the country, and the State Department last month hosted a donors' conference which pledged $3.2 billion in aid.
President Bill Clinton said while the conference was in progress that he was maintaining the ban, but there had been speculation that Christopher might lift it before leaving office.
The security lobby in the U.S. administration says Hizbollah and other guerrilla groups are still active in Lebanon, raising the potential threat of attacks or kidnappings against Americans.
The Beirut government says there have been no such actions against foreigners for years and that the ban is damaging business links between the United States and Lebanon.

But Dinger said: "We believe American businessmen can pursue business in Lebanon without travelling on American passports" -- an apparent reference to the fact that many are dual nationals who also hold Lebanese passports.
